title: Filter Cutoff
concept:
The Filter's most important control is the Cutoff frequency. It sets the boundary point where the filter starts to act. On a low-pass filter (the default), all frequencies below the cutoff pass through freely, while frequencies above are reduced.

At a high cutoff (around 8000 Hz) the filter is nearly open — you hear the full brightness of the sawtooth wave. As you lower the cutoff, you progressively remove the high harmonics, making the sound darker and warmer. At a very low cutoff (below 200 Hz) only the fundamental frequency remains — the sound becomes a near-pure sine.

This is one of the most expressive controls in synthesis. A slow sweep of the cutoff — from low to high — is the classic synthesizer 'filter sweep' sound you have heard in countless recordings.

Change the cutoff to around 300 Hz to hear the filter close down and darken the sound.

task.instruction: Lower the Filter's Cutoff to 300 Hz. Adjust the Cutoff knob on the Filter component and listen to the sound get darker as the high frequencies are removed.
